title: Neeraj Chopra Backs Team India as Asian Games Open in Aichi-Nagoya
excerpt: The Olympic champion, sidelined by an ankle ligament tear, took to X as the 20th Asian Games opened in Japan, expressing confidence the 500-strong Indian contingent would make the country proud.
body:
• Neeraj Chopra posted on X as the Games opened: "All my best wishes to Team India at the Asian Games 2026! I'm sure they will all make us proud."
  • The two-time Asian Games gold medallist and Olympic champion will miss the continental showpiece after an ankle ligament tear ended his 2026 season.
  • The 20th Asian Games run from September 19 to October 4 in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, with around 11,000 athletes from 45 nations competing across 43 sports.
  • India, fielding a 500-strong contingent led by flag-bearers Manu Bhaker and Pawan Sehrawat, aims to better its record Hangzhou 2023 haul of 106 medals.

Olympic champion Neeraj Chopra sent his best wishes to the Indian contingent on Saturday as the 20th Asian Games officially got underway in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan — even as an ankle injury keeps India's greatest track-and-field star out of the continental showpiece he has twice won.

"All my best wishes to Team India at the Asian Games 2026! I'm sure they will all make us proud."

— Neeraj Chopra, on X

An absent champion

Chopra, 28, will miss the Games after a ligament tear in his ankle during a training session ended his season — a cruel break that arrived just as he felt his form returning. "After a period of hard work, I finally felt I was gaining the momentum I had been looking for with a Season's Best throw in Lausanne," he wrote on social media last month. "Unfortunately, shortly after, I sustained a ligament tear in my ankle during training." The injury also cost him a place in the Diamond League finals despite having qualified. It is a significant absence for India's athletics campaign: Chopra won javelin gold at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics and silver at Paris 2024, and has been the face of Indian athletics for a generation.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=WFnQCg81TEg

A grand opening in Nagoya

The opening ceremony at the Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium formally marked the start of the Games, with Japan's Emperor Naruhito declaring the event open and contingents from 45 nations plus the OCA Refugee Team parading before the crowd. Olympic medallist Manu Bhaker and kabaddi star Pawan Sehrawat carried the Indian flag — Sehrawat stepping in after shot-putter Tajinderpal Singh Toor did not receive his ceremonial kit in time. Bhaker, a double bronze medallist at the Paris Olympics who will compete in the women's 10m air pistol, 25m pistol and mixed team events, said she felt "really proud, really honoured" to lead the contingent. India has sent around 500 athletes competing across 36 sports.

The medal target

India is looking to improve on its best-ever Asian Games performance at Hangzhou in 2023, where it won 106 medals, including 28 gold, 38 silver and 40 bronze. The campaign is already underway: India's women's cricket team reached the semifinals after defeating hosts Japan by eight wickets, and teqball player Quimcy D'Souza remains in contention for a bronze medal after losing her women's singles semifinal.

Following from afar

For the Indian diaspora — including a growing community in Japan itself — the Games offer two weeks of cheering across time zones, and Chopra's message, sent from the sidelines of an injury-enforced season, has the weight of a captain speaking to his team. His absence leaves a gap in the javelin, but the contingent's breadth, from shooting ranges to kabaddi mats, gives supporters plenty to follow.

What's ahead

With 469 gold medals to be decided across 43 sports before the closing ceremony on October 4, India's athletics squad will be watched closely to see who steps into the space Chopra's injury has left. The javelin thrower, meanwhile, has said his focus is on recovering well and returning stronger — Paris 2028 looms on his horizon.
